name: Saints Perpetua and Felicity
history: Two young mothers martyred together in the amphitheatre at Carthage: Perpetua, a well-born woman of twenty-two nursing her baby son, and Felicity, a slave who gave birth in prison days before she died. Perpetua kept a prison diary, one of the earliest writings we have by a Christian woman. Both are named in the Roman Canon.
life: In 203, under the Emperor Septimius Severus, a group of catechumens was arrested at Carthage: Perpetua, the slaves Felicity and Revocatus, Saturninus and Secundulus, and later their teacher Saturus, who gave himself up to share their fate. They were baptised while under guard. Perpetua’s father, a pagan, came again and again to beg her to sacrifice for the sake of her child. She pointed to a water jug and asked whether it could be called anything but what it was; nor, she said, could she be called anything but a Christian. In prison she recorded visions, among them a narrow ladder to heaven guarded by a serpent. Felicity, eight months pregnant, feared she would be left behind, since the law forbade the execution of pregnant women; she gave birth to a daughter, who was taken in by a Christian woman. On 7 March they were sent into the arena with wild beasts and then put to the sword, giving each other the kiss of peace.
prayerTo: Saints Perpetua and Felicity, noblewoman and slave, you went into the arena side by side, sisters in Christ. Pray for mothers and their children, for all who suffer for the faith, and for me, that I may never be ashamed to be called what I am, a Christian. Amen.
penance: Pray today for Christians in prison for their faith, and for mothers who are separated from their children. If you can, give to a charity that supports either.
meditation: Could this jug be called by any other name? So I cannot be called anything but what I am, a Christian. Where are you tempted to answer to another name?
